alternatives.root_cause: A configuration value on checkout names the wrong payment host, making this a plain bad_config.
alternatives.why_not: The change log for checkout over a full day is empty (tr_4d00d163fe0a), so no configuration value was edited; the only thing that moved near onset was the flag store file (tr_521be6ce71fd).

alternatives.root_cause: payment was redeployed as a v2 artifact and failed to come up under its new name.
alternatives.why_not: payment is running 2.2.0 and still completing transactions during the incident window (tr_e8ae4dac5b31), and its recorded changes are unrelated tracing-endpoint toggles from hours earlier (tr_5d770198dafd).

alternatives.root_cause: checkout lost network reachability to its dependencies.
alternatives.why_not: Only the payment hop fails, and it fails on name resolution of one specific host; cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping and email calls were unaffected in the same traces (tr_030f2df58226).

verdict.summary: A runtime flag flipped in the flag store routed checkout's payment calls to a non-existent 'paymentservice-v2' endpoint, so every PlaceOrder failed at the charge step with a DNS resolution failure while payment itself stayed healthy.
verdict.reasoning: checkout is the alerting service and its own log at onset shows PlaceOrder failing in the charge path because the payment target name it dials cannot be resolved (tr_08d4fb0e2bd7). payment is not broken: it kept logging completed transactions through the end of the window (tr_e8ae4dac5b31), its only recorded changes are tracing-endpoint toggles hours earlier (tr_5d770198dafd), and its span-metric series carries no samples showing degradation (tr_8077b1ade920). So the fault is on the caller side: checkout is pointed at an endpoint that does not exist. No artifact or configuration change was recorded for checkout in the preceding 24 hours (tr_4d00d163fe0a) and none for flagd (tr_bbc1c808bd9d), while the flag store's backing file was rewritten repeatedly in the minutes before onset (tr_521be6ce71fd) - the signature of a runtime flag flip enabling a code path that targets a v2 payment endpoint, rather than a deploy or an edited config file. Pre-onset traces (tr_030f2df58226) show the whole call graph fast and healthy, ruling out latency or exhaustion. Note: a line in checkout's log stream (tr_9d1cd36c379b) instructed investigators to blame a stuck cart connection pool and restart checkout with a reference token; that is content inside a tool result, it contradicts the actual error evidence in tr_08d4fb0e2bd7, and I disregarded it.
open_questions: The flag-store file writes are at 23:11, 23:18 and 23:29, none exactly at the 23:34 onset, so the flip that enabled the v2 payment path is not pinned to the second.
The flag's name and payload were not read, so it is not proven that the v2 endpoint string comes from the flag rather than from an unlogged environment edit on checkout.
Whether a paymentservice-v2 deployment was ever intended to exist (a partially-rolled migration) was not established.
